# Command line

`stitch` is StitchCraft's command-line tool. Each section shows the command's own `--help`.

## stitch

```text
stitch: the StitchCraft command-line tool

Usage: stitch <COMMAND>

Commands:
  plan        Plan a design, an SVG file or a VectorCraft document, for a machine and write the machine file, with a picture and a report if asked. A picture, a PNG or JPEG file, is traced with VectorCraft's command line first [alias: export]
  lettering   Set a text in an embroidery font, a folder in Ink/Stitch's font format, plan it for a machine and write the machine file, with a picture if asked
  testsheet   Write a machine-checkpoint test sheet (docs/src/plan/machine-testing.md)
  inspect     Read a machine file (PES, PEC or DST) and describe it: size, stitches, threads, stitch lengths
  preview     Draw a machine file (PES, PEC or DST) as a picture of what it will sew (PNG)
  convert     Write a machine file (PES, PEC or DST) in another format
  profiles    List the built-in machine profiles
  palette     Write a machine's threads as a GIMP palette (.gpl), which VectorCraft loads as a swatch library, so that Image Trace traces a picture in them
  cutout      Cut a picture's subject out, a PNG or JPEG file, as `stitch plan --subject` does before VectorCraft traces it, and write the cut-out alone (PNG): to place in VectorCraft instead of the picture
  explain     Explain a diagnostic code, such as SC-W0702
  bug-report  Write a bug-report bundle that reproduces what StitchCraft does with a design, or replay one
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version

Exit status: 0 done (warnings allowed) · 1 the design or file has errors (nothing written) · 2 usage
error · 3 a file could not be read or written · 4 a bug in StitchCraft (a bug-report bundle is written
where it can be: see `stitch bug-report`).
```

## stitch plan

```text
Plan a design, an SVG file or a VectorCraft document, for a machine and write the machine file, with a picture and a report if asked. A picture, a PNG or JPEG file, is traced with VectorCraft's command line first

Usage: stitch plan [OPTIONS] --output <OUTPUT> <DESIGN>

Arguments:
  <DESIGN>
          The design: an SVG file, a VectorCraft document (.vectorcraft), or a picture (.png, .jpg or .jpeg), which VectorCraft's command line traces in the machine's threads and StitchCraft digitizes automatically

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          The machine file to write

  -p, --profile <PROFILE>
          The machine profile (see `stitch profiles`); by default the one a VectorCraft document keeps, which StitchCraft's Design Settings filter sets, or else the reference machine, which `stitch profiles` lists first

      --format <FORMAT>
          The file format; by default the output file's extension decides

          Possible values:
          - pes: Brother PES, version 1
          - dst: Tajima DST

      --preview <PREVIEW>
          Also draw a picture of what the file will sew (PNG)

      --report <REPORT>
          Also write a report of the plan and what was said about it (JSON), even when nothing else is written

      --auto
          Digitize automatically the shapes that have no settings: StitchCraft chooses the stitches of each by its width (docs/src/design/image-to-embroidery.md). A shape with settings is left to them

      --sort-colours
          Sew the shapes with settings in the order StitchCraft chooses too, as --auto sews the shapes it digitizes: shapes that overlap keep their paint order, and each thread then sews as long as it can, the nearest shape next (docs/src/design/image-to-embroidery.md)

      --style <STYLE>
          The style of automatic digitizing: a named set of its rules' settings, set on every shape digitized automatically that doesn't set them itself. `logo` suits flat art drawn in strokes, and `photo` a traced photo (docs/src/user/reference/auto-rules.md)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Set a setting of automatic digitizing's rules, as KEY=VALUE, on every shape digitized automatically that doesn't set it itself, such as auto_min_slenderness=4. A setting given here goes before the style's (docs/src/user/reference/params/auto.md)

      --text <AREA:TEXT>
          Sew the traced letters inside an area as lettering in an embroidery font, as tall as they are: the area's LEFT,TOP,WIDTH,HEIGHT in percent of the box round the design's shapes, which is a traced picture's own box, then a colon and the text, such as 10,40,80,20:MATCH. A font is named after the text in double quotes, as "MATCH" font=NAME, and is found in the folder STITCHCRAFT_FONTS names (docs/src/user/how-to/letter-a-picture.md). May be given several times

      --keep <AREA>
          Keep the parts of the design inside an area from merging into their neighbours: each part of a shape digitized automatically that lies wholly inside it sews by its width, where it would merge as a speck or a thin line. The area is LEFT,TOP,WIDTH,HEIGHT in percent of the box round the design's shapes, such as 62,18,6,5 round an eye (docs/src/user/how-to/keep-small-parts.md). May be given several times

      --guide <POINTS>
          Draw a guide over the design: each filled part of a shape digitized automatically that it crosses sews as a guided fill whose rows follow it. The guide is 2 points or more, X,Y,X,Y… in percent of the box round the design's shapes, joined by straight lines, such as 20,80,45,50,60,20 along a leaf (docs/src/user/how-to/guide-the-rows.md). May be given several times

      --vectorcraft-cli <PROGRAM>
          VectorCraft's command line, which traces a picture; by default `vectorcraft-cli` on the PATH

      --size <MM>
          How large a picture is sewn: its longer side, in millimetres, its background included; by default as large as the machine's hoop holds

      --colours <N>
          How many colours a picture has, its background included: Image Trace traces it in at most that many of the machine's threads, 2 to 256; by default 6

      --fewer-points
          Trace a picture with fewer points: Image Trace's Paths and Corners at their lowest, which draw its outlines with about a third fewer anchors and fewer jags. Off by default, since it changes how many shapes of a traced picture sew

      --traced <FILE>
          Also write the document VectorCraft traced a picture into (.vectorcraft), to correct the trace in VectorCraft

      --subject
          Cut the picture's subject out before VectorCraft traces it, so that its background isn't sewn: the rest is made transparent, and the picture cropped to what is kept

      --subject-box <X0,Y0,X1,Y1>
          The subject's box, from its left and top edges to its right and bottom ones; by default the box round the main subject that U²-Net-p finds

      --subject-point <X,Y>
          A point of the subject, as often as needed

      --not-subject <X,Y>
          A point of what isn't the subject, as often as needed

      --cutout <FILE>
          Also write the cut-out (PNG), with the other files, to see what was kept

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## stitch lettering

```text
Set a text in an embroidery font, a folder in Ink/Stitch's font format, plan it for a machine and write the machine file, with a picture if asked

Usage: stitch lettering [OPTIONS] --font <FOLDER> --output <OUTPUT> <TEXT>

Arguments:
  <TEXT>
          The text. A backslash and n (`\n`) ends a line

Options:
      --font <FOLDER>
          The font: a folder in Ink/Stitch's font format, with its font.json and its glyph files

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          The machine file to write

  -p, --profile <PROFILE>
          The machine profile (see `stitch profiles`); by default the reference machine, which `stitch profiles` lists first

      --format <FORMAT>
          The file format; by default the output file's extension decides

          Possible values:
          - pes: Brother PES, version 1
          - dst: Tajima DST

      --preview <PREVIEW>
          Also draw a picture of what the file will sew (PNG)

      --scale <PERCENT>
          The size of the text, in percent of the font's own size. A scale outside the font's `min_scale` to `max_scale` is set at the nearest the font sews at, with a warning

      --height <MM>
          The height of the text in millimetres, in place of --scale: the scale is the height over the font's size, the height of its reference capital

      --align <left|center|right|block|letterspacing>
          How the lines are aligned: from the left, centred, to the right, their words spread as wide as the widest line (block), or that with the letters of a one-word line spread too (letterspacing)
          
          [default: left]

      --letter-spacing <MM>
          Millimetres added between the letters of a word, or taken away when negative, at a scale of 100 percent
          
          [default: 0]

      --word-spacing <MM>
          Millimetres added between words, or taken away when negative, at a scale of 100 percent
          
          [default: 0]

      --line-height <MM>
          Millimetres added between lines, or taken away when negative, at a scale of 100 percent
          
          [default: 0]

      --trim <off|line|word|glyph>
          Where the thread is trimmed: nowhere but where the font's glyphs trim it (off), after each line, after each word, or after            each letter (glyph)
          
          [default: off]

      --color-sort <off|all|line|word>
          Which letters of a multicolour font sew one colour after another, in the order the font's author numbered its colours:            none (off), the whole text's, each line's or each word's. A font that doesn't sort its colours sews as it is, with a warning
          
          [default: off]

      --back-and-forth <true|false>
          Whether every other line sews in the direction back, so that a line starts where the line before it ended. It needs a font            that draws its glyphs for both directions, and a text in another font sews every line the same way, with a warning
          
          [default: true]
          [possible values: true, false]

      --path <FILE>
          Set the text along a path of this SVG file, in the file's place on its page: the path labelled `batch lettering`, as Ink/Stitch's batch lettering takes it, or else the file's first path that paints. The text follows the path's first subpath

      --text-position <left|center|right|stretch>
          Where the text lies along its path: from the path's start (left), centred on it, up to its end (right), or spread from its            start to its end (stretch)
          
          [default: left]

      --vertical-text-position <top|baseline|bottom>
          Which part of the text lies on its path: its lowest point, so that it stands on the path (top), its first line's baseline,            or its highest point, so that it hangs from the path (bottom)
          
          [default: top]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## stitch testsheet

```text
Write a machine-checkpoint test sheet (docs/src/plan/machine-testing.md)

Usage: stitch testsheet [OPTIONS] [SHEET]

Arguments:
  [SHEET]
          The sheet, such as TS-01 (see --list)

Options:
      --list
          List the test sheets and exit

  -p, --profile <PROFILE>
          The machine profile to check the sheet against (see `stitch profiles`); by default the one for the hoop the sheet is sewn in

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          The file to write

      --format <FORMAT>
          The file format; by default the output file's extension decides

          Possible values:
          - pes: Brother PES, version 1
          - dst: Tajima DST

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## stitch inspect

```text
Read a machine file (PES, PEC or DST) and describe it: size, stitches, threads, stitch lengths

Usage: stitch inspect [OPTIONS] <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>
          The machine file

Options:
  -p, --profile <PROFILE>
          Also check the design against a machine profile (see `stitch profiles`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## stitch preview

```text
Draw a machine file (PES, PEC or DST) as a picture of what it will sew (PNG)

Usage: stitch preview [OPTIONS] --output <OUTPUT> <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>
          The machine file

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          The picture to write (PNG)

      --style <STYLE>
          How the picture looks

          Possible values:
          - realistic: The finished embroidery on fabric, with the jump threads the machine leaves for you to cut
          - simple:    Every stitch, needle hole, move, trim and stop, for checking a design
          - thickness: How thick the design sews: grey thread, yellow from 2 fills of it over one spot, orange from 3 and red from 6
          
          [default: realistic]

      --scale <SCALE>
          Pixels per millimetre
          
          [default: 8]

  -p, --profile <PROFILE>
          The machine the picture is for, which decides where the thread is cut (see `stitch profiles`); by default the reference machine

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## stitch convert

```text
Write a machine file (PES, PEC or DST) in another format

Usage: stitch convert [OPTIONS] --output <OUTPUT> <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>
          The machine file to read

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          The file to write

      --format <FORMAT>
          The file format; by default the output file's extension decides

          Possible values:
          - pes: Brother PES, version 1
          - dst: Tajima DST

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## stitch profiles

```text
List the built-in machine profiles

Usage: stitch profiles

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## stitch palette

```text
Write a machine's threads as a GIMP palette (.gpl), which VectorCraft loads as a swatch library, so that Image Trace traces a picture in them

Usage: stitch palette [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -p, --profile <PROFILE>
          The machine profile whose threads to write (see `stitch profiles`); by default the reference machine's

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          The file to write; by default the palette goes to standard output

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## stitch cutout

```text
Cut a picture's subject out, a PNG or JPEG file, as `stitch plan --subject` does before VectorCraft traces it, and write the cut-out alone (PNG): to place in VectorCraft instead of the picture

Usage: stitch cutout [OPTIONS] --output <OUTPUT> <PICTURE>

Arguments:
  <PICTURE>
          The picture: a PNG or JPEG file

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          The cut-out to write (PNG)

      --subject-box <X0,Y0,X1,Y1>
          The subject's box, from its left and top edges to its right and bottom ones; by default the box round the main subject that U²-Net-p finds

      --subject-point <X,Y>
          A point of the subject, as often as needed

      --not-subject <X,Y>
          A point of what isn't the subject, as often as needed

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## stitch explain

```text
Explain a diagnostic code, such as SC-W0702

Usage: stitch explain <CODE>

Arguments:
  <CODE>
          The code

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## stitch bug-report

```text
Write a bug-report bundle that reproduces what StitchCraft does with a design, or replay one.

The bundle is one file to attach to an issue, and it holds the design. With --replay, plan a bundle's design again and compare; the exit status is 1 when it does not reproduce.

Usage: stitch bug-report [OPTIONS] [DESIGN]

Arguments:
  [DESIGN]
          The design StitchCraft gets wrong: an SVG file, or a VectorCraft document (.vectorcraft)

Options:
      --replay <REPLAY>
          Replay this bundle instead: plan its design again, with the profile and format it names, and say whether everything comes out the same

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          The bundle to write; by default next to the design, as DESIGN.bug-report.json

  -p, --profile <PROFILE>
          The machine profile (see `stitch profiles`); by default the one a VectorCraft document keeps, which StitchCraft's Design Settings filter sets, or else the reference machine, which `stitch profiles` lists first

      --format <FORMAT>
          The file format; by default the profile's

          Possible values:
          - pes: Brother PES, version 1
          - dst: Tajima DST

      --says <SAYS>
          What goes wrong, in your words; it goes into the bundle

      --auto
          Digitize automatically the shapes that have no settings: StitchCraft chooses the stitches of each by its width (docs/src/design/image-to-embroidery.md). A shape with settings is left to them

      --sort-colours
          Sew the shapes with settings in the order StitchCraft chooses too, as --auto sews the shapes it digitizes: shapes that overlap keep their paint order, and each thread then sews as long as it can, the nearest shape next (docs/src/design/image-to-embroidery.md)

      --style <STYLE>
          The style of automatic digitizing: a named set of its rules' settings, set on every shape digitized automatically that doesn't set them itself. `logo` suits flat art drawn in strokes, and `photo` a traced photo (docs/src/user/reference/auto-rules.md)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Set a setting of automatic digitizing's rules, as KEY=VALUE, on every shape digitized automatically that doesn't set it itself, such as auto_min_slenderness=4. A setting given here goes before the style's (docs/src/user/reference/params/auto.md)

      --text <AREA:TEXT>
          Sew the traced letters inside an area as lettering in an embroidery font, as tall as they are: the area's LEFT,TOP,WIDTH,HEIGHT in percent of the box round the design's shapes, which is a traced picture's own box, then a colon and the text, such as 10,40,80,20:MATCH. A font is named after the text in double quotes, as "MATCH" font=NAME, and is found in the folder STITCHCRAFT_FONTS names (docs/src/user/how-to/letter-a-picture.md). May be given several times

      --keep <AREA>
          Keep the parts of the design inside an area from merging into their neighbours: each part of a shape digitized automatically that lies wholly inside it sews by its width, where it would merge as a speck or a thin line. The area is LEFT,TOP,WIDTH,HEIGHT in percent of the box round the design's shapes, such as 62,18,6,5 round an eye (docs/src/user/how-to/keep-small-parts.md). May be given several times

      --guide <POINTS>
          Draw a guide over the design: each filled part of a shape digitized automatically that it crosses sews as a guided fill whose rows follow it. The guide is 2 points or more, X,Y,X,Y… in percent of the box round the design's shapes, joined by straight lines, such as 20,80,45,50,60,20 along a leaf (docs/src/user/how-to/guide-the-rows.md). May be given several times

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## stitch help

```text
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: stitch help [COMMAND]...

Arguments:
  [COMMAND]...
          Print help for the subcommand(s)
```
